question: What has God's divine power given believers?
choices: All things that pertain to life and godliness
explanation: Peter says God's divine power has given everything needed for life and godliness.

question: What quality are believers told to add first to their faith?
explanation: Peter begins the chain of spiritual growth by saying to add virtue to faith.

question: What does Peter say believers should make sure?
explanation: Peter tells them to give diligence to make their calling and election sure.

question: What event does Peter refer to when he says they were eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty?
choices: The feeding of the five thousand
explanation: Peter recalls hearing the Father's voice on the holy mount at the transfiguration.

question: How does Peter say prophecy came in old time?
choices: Holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Ghost
explanation: Peter says prophecy did not come by the will of man. Holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

question: What will false teachers secretly introduce?
explanation: Peter says false teachers will secretly bring in destructive heresies.

question: Whom does Peter say God spared as a preacher of righteousness?
explanation: Noah is cited as an example of God's rescue of the righteous.

question: Whom did God deliver when He condemned Sodom and Gomorrah?
explanation: Peter highlights Lot as righteous and rescued from the filthy conduct of the wicked.

question: What do false teachers promise while they themselves are servants of corruption?
explanation: Peter says they promise liberty while being slaves of corruption.

question: To what does Peter compare those who turn back after knowing the way of righteousness?
choices: A sheep returning to the fold
A dog returning to its vomit
explanation: Peter uses the proverb of a dog returning to its vomit to picture returning to corruption.

question: What kind of people does Peter say will come in the last days?
explanation: Peter warns that scoffers will come walking after their own lusts.

question: How does Peter describe the Lord's timing?
choices: One day is with the Lord as a thousand years
explanation: Peter reminds believers that God's perspective on time differs from ours.

question: Peter says the Lord is not slack about His promise. Why does He wait?
choices: Because He is longsuffering and not willing that any should perish
explanation: Peter says the Lord is not slack. He is longsuffering and wants all to come to repentance.

question: How will the day of the Lord come?
choices: As a sign in the stars
As a thief in the night
explanation: Peter says the day of the Lord will come unexpectedly like a thief.

question: In what are believers told to grow?
choices: Grace and the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
explanation: Peter closes by urging believers to grow in grace and in the knowledge of Christ.

question: Who calls himself a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ at the start of this letter?
explanation: The letter opens: Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ.

question: What did the voice from heaven call Jesus?
explanation: The voice said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

question: Into what kingdom will an entrance be ministered abundantly to those who do these things?
choices: The everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ
The kingdom of the first resurrection
explanation: An entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

question: What does Peter say believers should add to brotherly kindness?
explanation: Add to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness charity.

question: What does Peter say of the person who lacks these things?
choices: He is dead in his sins
He is blind and cannot see afar off
He is cast out of the church
He is deaf to the word
explanation: He that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off.

question: What has the person who lacks these things forgotten?
choices: That he was called by name
That he was purged from his old sins
explanation: He hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.

question: If these things are in believers and abound, what will they not be?
explanation: They make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

question: What word does Peter use for his own body, which he must shortly put off?
explanation: Peter says he must shortly put off this his tabernacle, as the Lord Jesus Christ had shewed him.

question: Where were Peter and the others when they heard the voice from heaven?
explanation: This voice which came from heaven we heard, when we were with him in the holy mount.

question: What does Peter say they had NOT followed when they made known the power and coming of Christ?
explanation: We have not followed cunningly devised fables, but were eyewitnesses of his majesty.

question: To what does Peter compare the word of prophecy?
choices: A light that shineth in a dark place
explanation: We have a more sure word of prophecy, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place.

question: By the great and precious promises, believers might become partakers of what?
explanation: By these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.

question: If believers do these things, what does Peter say they shall never do?
explanation: Give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall.

question: From whom did Christ receive honour and glory, according to Peter?
explanation: He received from God the Father honour and glory, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory.

question: Until what does Peter say believers should take heed to the word of prophecy?
choices: Until all the prophets are fulfilled
Until the day dawn and the day star arise in their hearts
explanation: Take heed until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts.

question: What does Peter say he will not be negligent to do, even though they already know these things?
choices: Put them always in remembrance of these things
explanation: I will not be negligent to put you always in remembrance of these things, though ye know them.

question: Peter says no prophecy of the scripture is of what?
explanation: No prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.

question: Through the knowledge of whom are grace and peace multiplied?
choices: God, and of Jesus our Lord
explanation: Grace and peace be multiplied unto you through the knowledge of God, and of Jesus our Lord.

question: From what have believers escaped through the promises?
choices: The corruption of the world through lust
explanation: Having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.

question: What does Peter say to add to knowledge?
explanation: And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience.

question: What does Peter say to add to patience?
explanation: And to patience godliness.

question: As long as Peter is in his tabernacle, what does he think it meet to do?
choices: Stir them up by putting them in remembrance
explanation: I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance.

question: In what truth does Peter say his readers are established?
explanation: Though ye know them, and be established in the present truth.

question: From where did the voice that said "This is my beloved Son" come?
explanation: There came such a voice to him from the excellent glory.

question: To what has God's divine power called believers?
explanation: Through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue.

question: To what word does Peter say believers do well to take heed?
choices: The more sure word of prophecy
explanation: We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed.

question: Through whose righteousness have believers obtained like precious faith?
choices: God and our Saviour Jesus Christ
explanation: Like precious faith through the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ.

question: What does Peter tell believers to add to virtue?
explanation: Add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge.

question: Which prophet loved the wages of unrighteousness?
explanation: They follow the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness.

question: What rebuked the madness of the prophet Balaam?
choices: A dumb ass speaking with man's voice
explanation: The dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet.

question: What did God turn Sodom and Gomorrah into?
explanation: God turned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes, condemning them with an overthrow.

question: What did God bring upon the world of the ungodly in Noah's day?
explanation: God spared not the old world, but saved Noah, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly.

question: What animal is described as washed and then returning to wallowing in the mire?
explanation: The true proverb says, the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.

question: What will the false teachers deny?
explanation: They shall privily bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them.

question: Through what do the false teachers, with feigned words, make merchandise of believers?
explanation: Through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you.

question: Where did God deliver the angels that sinned to be reserved unto judgment?
explanation: God cast the angels that sinned down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment.

question: How was Lot's righteous soul affected by living among the wicked?
choices: It was vexed from day to day
explanation: That righteous man dwelling among them vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds.

question: What did the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah make them to those who would live ungodly after?
explanation: God made them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly.

question: To what does Peter compare the false teachers who promise much and give nothing?
choices: Wells without water and clouds carried with a tempest
explanation: These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest.

question: What does Peter say would have been better for them than turning from the holy commandment?
choices: Not to have known the way of righteousness
To have died in their sins
To have left the church earlier
explanation: It had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than after they have known it to turn from the holy commandment.

question: Whose son was Balaam, according to Peter?
explanation: Peter says Balaam was the son of Bosor.

question: What is reserved for ever for these false teachers?
explanation: They are wells without water; to them the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.

question: What does the Lord know how to do with the godly and the unjust?
choices: Gather the godly and scatter the unjust
Forgive the godly and forget the unjust
Test the godly and warn the unjust
Deliver the godly and reserve the unjust for judgment
explanation: The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished.

question: What does Peter say their eyes are full of?
explanation: They have eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin.

question: What will happen to the way of truth because many follow their pernicious ways?
choices: It will be evil spoken of
explanation: Many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of.

question: If those who escaped the pollutions of the world are entangled again, what does Peter say?
choices: The latter end is worse than the beginning
They shall be cast out at once
explanation: If they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning.

question: To what does Peter liken those who speak evil of things they understand not?
explanation: These, as natural brute beasts, speak evil of the things that they understand not.

question: What number of person was Noah, when God saved him?
explanation: God saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness.

question: What do angels, greater in power and might, not bring against them before the Lord?
explanation: Angels, which are greater in power and might, bring not railing accusation against them before the Lord.

question: What do these false teachers count pleasure?
explanation: They count it pleasure to riot in the daytime.

question: Who does Peter say were among the people in old time, as false teachers shall be among you?
explanation: There were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you.

question: Of whom are the flesh-following teachers not afraid to speak evil?
explanation: They despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.

question: What does Peter call these teachers, whose heart is exercised with covetous practices?
explanation: An heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children.

question: What kind of words do they speak when they allure those who had escaped error?
explanation: They speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh.

question: What does Peter call them as they feast with believers?
explanation: Spots they are and blemishes, sporting themselves with their own deceivings while they feast with you.

question: Of whom is a man brought in bondage, according to Peter?
explanation: Of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage.

question: What do the scoffers say?
choices: Who is the Lord that we should obey him?
Where is the promise of his coming?
Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die
There is no resurrection of the dead
explanation: Scoffers shall come saying, Where is the promise of his coming?

question: What do believers look for, according to God's promise?
choices: New heavens and a new earth
explanation: We, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.

question: How did the world that then was perish?
explanation: The world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished.

question: Which fellow apostle does Peter call "our beloved brother"?
explanation: Peter says, even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you.

question: What will the heavens do when the day of the Lord comes?
choices: Pass away with a great noise
explanation: In the day of the Lord the heavens shall pass away with a great noise.

question: What shall melt with fervent heat in the day of the Lord?
explanation: The elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.

question: What are the heavens and the earth that are now kept in store reserved unto?
explanation: The heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment.

question: After what do the scoffers of the last days walk?
explanation: There shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts.

question: What reason do the scoffers give for saying that things have not changed?
choices: No prophet has spoken in their lifetime
The fathers fell asleep and all things continue
explanation: Since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.

question: Who twist the hard-to-understand things in Paul's letters, to their own destruction?
explanation: Some things are hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.

question: What does Peter tell believers to account the longsuffering of the Lord to be?
explanation: Account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation.

question: How does Peter say believers should be found by the Lord?
choices: In peace, without spot, and blameless
explanation: Be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless.

question: What does Peter say he stirs up by way of remembrance?
explanation: In both letters, I stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance.

question: Whose words does Peter want his readers to remember, besides the commandment of the apostles?
explanation: That ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and of the commandment of us the apostles.

question: What does Peter say the scoffers are willingly ignorant of?
choices: That the Lord would come again
That the heavens and earth were made by the word of God
explanation: They willingly are ignorant that by the word of God the heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and in the water.

question: Peter warns believers not to fall from what?
explanation: Beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness.

question: What does Peter say believers are doing as they look for the coming of the day of God?
explanation: Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God.

question: What will be burned up in the day of the Lord, along with the earth?
explanation: The earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.

question: What manner of persons does Peter say believers ought to be?
choices: In all holy conversation and godliness
explanation: What manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness.

question: What shall the heavens on fire be, in the day of God?
explanation: The heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat.

question: According to what was Paul given wisdom to write?
explanation: Our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you.

question: To whom does Peter ascribe glory both now and for ever?
choices: Our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ
explanation: To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen.

question: The heavens and earth are reserved against the day of judgment and perdition of whom?
explanation: Reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.
